findings.original: the smallness of that aliquot part of any produce
findings.rewrite: the smallness of that aliquot part [equal fraction] of any produce
findings.problem: The gloss says the two parts are equal, but the worker's share and the remainder are not; the glossary was corrected to "fractional part" for this reason.
findings.fix: Change the bracket to "aliquot part [fractional part]".

findings.original: the burden falls on the labourer, in the increased exploitation of whom the capitalist looks for his indemnification.
findings.rewrite: the burden falls on the worker, since the capitalist looks to the worker’s increased exploitation to make up his loss.
findings.problem: Marx's relative clause describes where the capitalist seeks compensation; "since" turns it into the reason the burden falls on the worker.
findings.fix: the burden falls on the worker, in whose increased exploitation the capitalist looks for compensation.

findings.original: Though the same quantity of labour adds always to its products only the same sum of new value, still the old capital value
findings.rewrite: So although the same quantity of labor always adds only the same sum of new value
findings.problem: "So" adds an inference from the previous sentence that Marx does not mark.
findings.fix: Delete "So": "Although the same quantity of labor always adds only the same sum of new value ...".

notes_review: Most logged calls are sound (Dogberry identification, "minimum of wages", literal retranslation of the Say brackets, unmatched marks kept). Note 12's gloss "aliquot part [equal fraction]" goes against the corrected glossary entry, and it is fixed here.
summary: Fidelity is high: numbers, citations, attributions, French text and Marx's irony (Rumford, Say, MacCulloch) all survive, with only three small slips in a gloss and two added logical links. The prose is plain and readable, and the glossary and spelling are applied consistently.
